payload.text: E-01 (6 Oct 2026, before any final evaluation of any root): From 13:26 UTC OpenRouter refused every request with HTTP 403 'Workspace monthly budget of $60.00 exceeded' (an account setting outside the registered $145 project ceiling). Under the inherited rule each refusal was settled at the full $0.05 reservation and failed only its proposal, so affected LLM arms exhausted their $0.75 caps on refusals and ended at the candidate safety ceiling, and affected zero-shot stages stopped; these are infrastructure failures, not treatment outcomes. The investigator raised the workspace budget and chose recovery by rerun (same precedent as A/B amendment 02). Changes: (1) every LLM or zero-shot arm whose PAUSES.jsonl records an HTTP 403 is set aside to <root>/superseded_E01/ (retained, never edited) together with the root's SELECTION.json and, when the LLM arm is set aside, its pair.json; GP arms are untouched; (2) the launcher re-certifies the fresh LLM arm against the unchanged GP arm (initialization is deterministic and makes no API calls; an arm that already holds its 12 initialization records or a terminal event is reused, not rerun); (3) set-aside arms rerun from scratch with fresh journals under identical treatment and caps; (4) any future HTTP 403 halts the launcher instead of failing a proposal. The global ledger keeps the conservative $0.05 charges for the refusals (about $7.70), so the $145 ceiling remains conservative. The analysis reports results with and without the rerun roots. HTTP 404 'no allowed providers' errors at the end of peak windows (roots 15-19, 2-4 per arm) were handled by the registered rule and are not affected.
